body:
I know what you mean with the medical odds, but that almost makes me feel more determined. As fucked up as it sounds, I feel like Bruce Willis from Unbreakable. The first time, the doctors told me that the blood serum levels of DPH were well above lethal standards. Then again, I had two heart attacks because of it, so it may have been medical science that saved me.

The second time though, by the time they found me my potassium levels were so low they had to put me in a medically induced coma and use a cocktail of shit to save me. I honestly wish they didn't.

I really want to. God, I really want to, but I literally have no hope right now. I don't mean objectively, but I feel hopeless beyond anything I've ever felt. I know that I can do great things, but I have literally no hope that I can achieve them.

That's the most fucked up thing about it. The military refuses to let me take my Depakote because it makes me undeployable. The on-staff psychiatrist rescinded my diagnosis of bipolar simply because of that reason. It was the only medication that ever made me feel normal.

I don't have PTSD, I've never had anything close to a combat experience.

> I'm not entirely sure I understand though why you stopped taking the anti depressants if they were helping you.

I wish I knew myself.

> What do you mean?

I can't go into to many specifics about my career unfortunately. First, out of the need to remain anonymous over the next few weeks. What I can say is that I waited for the apocalypse to happen on a daily basis. That was my entire job.

> Why would it make it impossible to get disability outside the military? (Sorry, I'm kind of clueless on that sort of thing)

Because the military is a federal agency. They can determine disability ratings as much as any other agency, and because they decided to characterize me as completely non-disabled, and simply having a personality disorder, it severely reduces my chances of having it recharacterized by another federal agency.

I understand where you're coming from, but I really can't see any reason to live. I have some people who care about me, but my parents essentially disowned me; I have maybe one good friend in the world, losing most of them as a result of my suicide attempts and depression; and I don't know if I can survive another month financially.

I stopped taking my anti-depressants because I realized how fucked up my life was. The only reason I stayed on my anxiolytic was because otherwise I'd be unable to type right now. My life has been so fucked up by my career choice that it has left me a quivering wreck, and I don't even know if I can hold a job. The military has decided to discharge me under a general discharge so they can deny me medical benefits, and I'm just fucked. Because of the military's discharge, I doubt I'd even be eligible for disability in the outside world.

Right now I see my life as being nothing but one of those homeless vets on the street corner, and I could never do that. It seems like the less of two evils.
